about: The setup list a project manager works down at a site: the platform's own steps, in its own order, with the exact titles the platform shows (apps/api/src/setup/setup-checklist.ts; the build checks every title against that file). The site packs print the twelve steps from here, so a title can only be typed once. 'when' says which kits show the step: the platform leaves a step out when it does not apply to the site. The words under 'see' and 'ifnot' are the platform's own sentences where it has them (in italics).

steps.title: Order form signed and data terms agreed
steps.do: Nothing goes into a customer's building until the order form is signed and the data terms are agreed. Greecon keeps the papers; the platform cannot see a signature, so you write down that they exist. In the box above the button write **who signed for the customer and on what date** (for example *Signed for the hotel by Besa Krasniqi on 19 October*): it cannot be left empty. Press **{{ui.papers_signed}}**. Do this at the office, and bring copies on install day.
steps.see: The step turns **{{ui.status_done}}**: *Signed and agreed.*, with your name, the time and what you wrote. They are on the handover sheet.
steps.ifnot: Until it is done, commissioning stays grey. The button will not work while the box is empty. If a paper turns out to be wrong, press **{{ui.reopen}}** (if the site had been commissioned, that is taken back too).

steps.title: Prices from the customer's bills
steps.do: Open **{{ui.enter_prices}}** (once something is entered it is called *Prices and baseline*; the same form is on the site's page). Enter the currency; the electricity price per kWh from the latest bill; what is paid for energy sent to the grid (leave it blank if nothing is paid); the water price per m³; a typical month before (the kWh bought and the m³ of water, from last year's bills); where those numbers came from; whether the site cannot send energy to the grid (tick it if the plant is zero-export); and the time zone, `Europe/Tirane`. Press **{{ui.save}}**.
steps.see: The step turns **{{ui.status_done}}** and lists the prices, for example *Electricity: N ALL per kWh* (and *Water: N ALL per m³* where the site has a water flow reading).
steps.ifnot: It stays **{{ui.status_todo}}** and says *Not set: Greecon shows kWh but cannot say what they are worth.* That is allowed: this step is optional and does not hold up commissioning, and without a price Greecon shows kWh only. Without the typical month before, no comparison is shown, which is correct.

steps.title: Install the box
steps.do: Press **{{ui.add_box}}** and copy the line it shows (shown once, works once, lasts seven days). Run it on the box exactly as shown. This is done at the office, before install day.
steps.see: **{{ui.status_done}}**, with the box's name, its version and *Heard from N seconds ago.* You do not press anything to make it so: the platform saw the box.
steps.ifnot:
- *Waiting for the install command to be run on the box.* The line has not been run yet.
- *The box has its credential but has not reported yet.* Wait a minute and check the network cable.
- *Last heard from N ago: it is offline.* Check the box's power, the network cable and the site's internet. On the box: `greecon-edge status` and `journalctl -u greecon-edge -n 50 --no-pager`.
- *Online, but its clock is N minutes fast* (or slow). Run `sudo timedatectl set-ntp true`.

steps.title: Where each device is on the network
steps.do:
Press **{{ui.find_equipment}}**. Nobody types an IP address, a port or a unit number here.

- The box looks at the site's own network (local private addresses only, port 502, about a minute) and only reads. The page says *The box is looking at the network now.* and updates by itself. The platform recognises what answered and fills in at once only what is certain: a device with no address, found at the kit's own number. The rest waits for you.
- A device **{{ui.found_found}}** but not filled in (another address, another number, another meter model): read the line and, if it makes sense, press **{{ui.use_this_address}}** (or *Use these N addresses*). An optional device the site does not have: press **{{ui.site_does_not_have}}**.
- The soil probe, the weather sensor and a battery are entered by hand: under the device open **{{ui.enter_address_by_hand}}** (soil probe 6, weather sensor 7).
- Box not on your network (a desk rehearsal), or a converter on another port: open **{{ui.i_know_the_address}}**, type its address (and its port, if not 502), and press **{{ui.look_at_this_address}}**.
steps.see: Each device gets a line in plain words: **{{ui.found_set}}** (found, address filled in), **{{ui.found_found}}**, **{{ui.found_not_found}}**, **{{ui.found_not_sure}}** or **{{ui.found_by_hand}}**. When it worked the step is **{{ui.status_done}}** (*Every device has an address.*), and the button reads **{{ui.look_again}}**.
steps.ifnot:
- **{{ui.found_not_found}}**: *Nothing that looks like an Eastron meter answers at unit 2. Check the address set on it, the speed, and the A and B wires.* An optional device the site does not have: press **{{ui.site_does_not_have}}**.
- **{{ui.found_not_sure}}**: Greecon will not guess, because a wrong guess could swap the grid meter and the solar meter. Read each device's label, use **{{ui.enter_address_by_hand}}** under each with the number on its label, then **{{ui.look_again}}**. Numbers are set at the office: a part with a wrong number goes back there.
- *No Modbus converter answered on this network:* check that the converter is on and plugged into the same router as the box. *A converter answers at 192.168.1.50, but nothing answers behind it:* check each meter's address, the speed and the A and B wires. *All answered with exactly the same words:* the converter is not in gateway mode. *The box did not pick this up:* check that it shows as online in the step above.
- Readings that stop after it had worked: the router may have given the converter a new address. Press **{{ui.find_equipment}}**, then **{{ui.use_this_address}}**.

steps.title: Which register holds which reading
steps.do:
The Eastron meters and the pump contact module need nothing typed. For the 4 to 20 mA module the page asks, for each transmitter, only for the range printed on its label, in the label's own words:

- **{{ui.range_level}}** (input 1): the **{{ui.range_on_label}}**, for example 5, its **{{ui.unit_on_label}}** (metres, or bar) and **{{ui.tank_height}}** in metres, for example 4: from the bottom to the top of the water when full.
- **{{ui.range_pressure}}** (input 2): the **{{ui.top_of_range}}** in bar; 10 is usual.
- **{{ui.range_flow}}** (input 3): the **{{ui.top_of_range}}** in litres a minute.

Greecon works out the register and the scale. For a transmitter the site does not have (no flow meter), tick **{{ui.not_fitted}}**: Greecon asks first, then takes the reading and its history away. Press **{{ui.save_the_ranges}}**.

Equipment Greecon does not know (the soil probe, the weather sensor, a battery) is mapped by hand, from the maker's register table: under the reading press **{{ui.choose_the_register}}** and fill in the register kind (**{{ui.register_input}}** for a manual's 3xxxx, **{{ui.register_holding}}** for 4xxxx), the address (counted from zero: 30053 is address 52, 40001 is address 0), the kind of number (and which half comes first), how it becomes the reading (**{{ui.multiply_and_add}}**, or **{{ui.straight_line}}**) and which part of the value. Press **{{ui.save_the_register}}**.
steps.see: **{{ui.status_done}}**: *Every reading is tied to a register.* Under each transmitter the form says what it set, for example *Set now: 4 mA is 0 % and 20 mA is 125 %.* (0 to 5 m in a tank 4 m tall); the tank level is a percentage of the tank, so a full tank reads 100.
steps.ifnot: *N readings not tied to a register yet*, each marked *Needs the range printed on the transmitter's label.* (the 4 to 20 mA module) or *No register chosen.* (equipment Greecon does not know). A transmitter shorter than the tank is refused: *The transmitter reads up to 3 m and the tank is 4 m tall: it cannot see the top of the water. Fit a transmitter with a longer range.* A reading the site does not have holds the list here: tick **{{ui.not_fitted}}**, or press **{{ui.site_does_not_have}}** (step 4) for an optional device.

steps.title: Every device answers the box
steps.do: Nothing to press: the platform does this one by itself once the box is online and each device has its address and registers. Wait a minute.
steps.see: Each device shows **{{ui.status_done}}**: *Answering (N readings).* On the box, `greecon-edge status` lists each device as **ok**.
steps.ifnot: The device shows **{{ui.status_attention}}** with the reason in words, for example *no answer from 192.168.1.50:502 (unit 2).* Look in this order: the converter's address may have changed (press **{{ui.find_equipment}}** again, then **{{ui.use_this_address}}**); the number on the device's label against the install card; the speed at the converter; A and B swapped on the data cable; the converter not in gateway mode. Nothing answers at all: the converter is off, or it is on another network than the box. Test one register from the box with `greecon-edge modbus-test` (see the box commands): if it prints *Could not read*, the problem is the wiring or the settings, not Greecon.

steps.title: Readings arrive and look right
steps.do: Nothing to press. Look at each reading: is it a number you believe?
steps.see: Each reading shows **{{ui.status_done}}** with its value and age, for example *N %, 4 seconds ago*, and the step says *Every reading is arriving and could be real.* **{{ui.reading_pump}}** reads 1 while the pump runs and 0 while it is stopped.
steps.ifnot: *No reading yet*: wait a minute. *Last reading N ago. It has stopped arriving*: a device or the converter lost power, or a cable came loose. A value that cannot be real says so, for example *-31.2 cannot be a tank level (0 to 100). Check the register address, the scale or the sensor.* On a transmitter a reading below zero is nearly always a wire that has come off (the module then reads 0, below the 4 mA of an empty tank); one far too high is a range or tank height typed wrongly: give the ranges again (step 5).

steps.title: Someone is told when the site needs attention
steps.do: Open **{{ui.who_is_told}}**. **{{ui.add_a_person}}** for each name from the survey, in the order they should be told (each needs an email, a mobile number with its country code such as `+355 69 123 4567`, or both; give everyone an email address as well as a number). Press **{{ui.save_the_list}}**. Press **{{ui.send_test_message}}** beside each person and ask them whether it arrived: in the inbox, not in spam; on the phone. Tell each person that every alert message has an *I have seen this* link: one tap, no sign-in, and it stops the message going on to the next person. Give a login of their own (the Operator role) only to those who should also look at the screens. Then, back on the setup list, press **{{ui.i_checked_this}}**.
steps.see: After the test: *A test message was sent N ago. Greecon cannot tell whether it was read.* After you press the button: **{{ui.status_done}}**, *A test message reached the person on the list.* The button stays grey until the list has someone on it and a test has been sent.
steps.ifnot:
- *This Greecon platform is not set up to send messages:* tell the founder; the email service must be switched on before a site can be commissioned.
- *Nobody is set to be told:* add the people.
- *Nobody on the list has an email address* (or a phone number): add one for each person.
- A message that did not arrive: look at **{{ui.what_was_sent}}** under **{{ui.who_is_told}}**, check the address and the country code, and ask about spam.
- *Test messages are limited to 6 an hour.* Wait and try again.

steps.title: Grid meter direction checked
steps.do: Greecon cannot see which way the meter's clamps point. With the sun down or the solar switched off, switch on a known load (a kettle or a heater). **{{ui.reading_grid_import}} must go up.** If **{{ui.reading_grid_export}}** goes up instead, the clamps are the wrong way round: the electrician turns them (with the lock-out on) and you check again. Then press **{{ui.i_checked_this}}** with a note of what you saw.
steps.see: Before: **{{ui.status_todo}}**, *Greecon cannot see which way the meter's clamps point.* After you confirm: **{{ui.status_done}}**, *Checked on site,* with your name and the time.
steps.ifnot: Import and export swapped: the clamps are the wrong way round. The electrician turns them; you repeat the check. A reversed clamp swaps what the site buys with what it sells, and every figure with it.

steps.title: Alert limits agreed with the customer
steps.do: The step lists each reading that has limits, with what applies. Go through them with the customer and agree numbers they would act on. To change one, open the **{{ui.standard}}** drop-down beside the reading (it says *1 set*, *2 set* once changed), type the numbers and press **{{ui.save_limits}}**. When they are agreed, press **{{ui.i_checked_this}}**.
steps.see: Each reading with limits is listed with its numbers, for example *Tank level: Critical below 15 % (standard); Low below 35 % (standard).* After you confirm: **{{ui.status_done}}**, *Checked on site.*
steps.ifnot: The standard limits apply until you change them: tank **Critical below 15 percent** (an Act now alert) and **Low below 35 percent** (a Check today alert); pump **No flow at or below 0.2 litres a minute** (an Act now alert once it has held for 30 seconds, raised only when the box reads both a flow and the pump's running state); battery **Low below 25 percent**. **Start irrigating below** has no standard value: Greecon gives no irrigation advice until the grower's own value is entered.

steps.title: Electrical work done by a licensed electrician
steps.do: Fitting meters in a board and wiring transmitters and contacts is the **licensed electrician's** work, under the customer's lock-out. When the electrician has finished and the lock-out is removed, ask for their name and licence number, photograph the wiring, the labels and the displays, and check that the lock-out has been removed. Then write in the box the electrician's **name and licence number** (for example *Arben Hoxha, licence E-1234*), or that no electrical work was needed: it cannot be left empty. Press **{{ui.electrical_work_done}}**.
steps.see: The step turns **{{ui.status_done}}**: *Done by a licensed electrician.*, with your name, the time and what you wrote (they are on the handover sheet). The platform does not check the licence: what you write is the record.
steps.ifnot: Until it is done, commissioning stays grey. Do not press the button while the work is open or the lock-out is still on. The button will not work while the box is empty.

steps.title: Commissioned
steps.do: Greyed out until every other step is done (optional steps do not hold it). Then it says: *On site, compare what Greecon shows with what you can see: the meter's own display, the tank, the pressure gauge. When they agree, confirm here.* Do the commissioning tests in this pack, write the pairs of numbers on the record, then press **{{ui.commission_this_site}}** with a note.
steps.see: The progress line reads **{{step:12}}.**, your name and the date are on the handover sheet, and **{{ui.handover_sheet}}** appears.
steps.ifnot: While it is grey it says *N steps above must be done first.* and *Finish the steps above.* Finish them first.
